title: Counterclaims against an opposing party
summary: A counterclaim is a claim against an opposing party. Rule 13 distinguishes compulsory claims arising from the relevant transaction or occurrence from permissive claims that may be asserted without that connection.
notes: A claim’s procedural classification and its jurisdictional basis are separate. The pre-§ 1367 ancillary-jurisdiction cases must be read alongside the later statute.

sections.Meaning: A counterclaim is a claim against an opposing party. Rule 13 distinguishes compulsory claims arising from the relevant transaction or occurrence from permissive claims that may be asserted without that connection.
sections.How to work through the question: Identify the opposing party, the factual relationship, the time the claim existed, and any applicable exception. Then examine jurisdiction. Heyward-Robinson illustrates both the breadth and the disagreement surrounding a logical-relationship approach.
